1 Overview

This notebook implements Step 2 of the EMAuxiliary Workflow: evaluating candidate auxiliary variables in EMA data.
Auxiliary variables help make the missing-at-random (MAR) assumption more plausible and can reduce bias due to prompt nonresponse.

What this notebook does 1. Data prep for auxiliary variable evaluation: Classify each auxiliary as within-, between-, or mixed-level variables (based on ICC). Decompose and standardize variables into within- and between-person parts.
3. Estimate multilevel logistic models predicting missingness 4. Compute within- and between-level correlations between auxiliary variables and focal variables. 4. Generate a detailed summary table to evaluate auxiliaries. 4. Rank auxiliaries.

Output
Produces interactive and static tables summarizing each auxiliary’s predictive utility and conceptual relevance.
These results guide the selection of auxiliaries to include in Step 3 (Modeling with EMAuxiliary).

Dependencies
R (≥ 4.2), dplyr, tidyr, lme4, broom.mixed, gt, DT.

For background and installation instructions, see the README.

2 Introduction

This tutorial guides you step-by-step through the evaluation of auxiliary variables in Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) data.
Auxiliary variables can improve the plausibility of missing-at-random (MAR) assumptions and reduce bias due to nonresponse.

Each section explains what to do, why it matters, and how to interpret the results.

Packages required:
Install these before running:
install.packages(c("lme4", "broom.mixed", "dplyr", "tidyr", "gt", "DT"))

2.1 Step 1: Load Your EMA Dataset

What to do: Replace the file path below with your own dataset.
Your data must include: - an ID variable identifying individuals
- a missingness variable (1 = missing prompt, 0 = completed prompt)
- one or more candidate auxiliary variables
- one or more focal variables from your model of interest

# 🔄 EDIT THIS LINE: Replace with your real dataset path
# Example:
# ema_df <- read.csv("your_data.csv")

2.1.1 Optional: Try the Example Dataset (for testing only)

If you don’t yet have your data ready, uncomment and run this section to create a tiny toy dataset. It includes a pure within variable (day_of_study) and a pure between variable (age). Remember to comment this back out when you switch to your own data.

set.seed(123)
ema_df <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:6, each = 5),
  time_of_day = runif(30, 6, 22),
  day_of_study = rep(1:5, times = 6),
  weekend = sample(0:1, 30, replace = TRUE),
  negative_affect = rnorm(30),
  physical_activity = rnorm(30),
  sedentary_behavior = rnorm(30),
  completion_time = runif(30, 2, 8),
  prompt_delay = runif(30, 0, 2)
)
ema_df$age <- rep(sample(45:75, 6, replace = TRUE), each = 5)

# Small missingness model signal: longer completion_time and weekends increase missingness
linpred <- (ema_df$completion_time - mean(ema_df$completion_time)) * 0.3 +
           0.25 * (ema_df$weekend - mean(ema_df$weekend))
ema_df$missed_prompt <- rbinom(30, 1, plogis(linpred))

2.2 Step 2: Define Your Variables

What to do: Insert the column names from your dataset.
- aux_vars: candidate auxiliaries to screen
- focal_vars: outcome/predictors from your main model (used for interpretive correlations)
- id_var: person identifier
- missing_var: prompt-level missingness indicator (1 = missed prompt)

# 🔄 EDIT THESE NAMES to match your dataset
aux_vars <- c(
  "time_of_day", "day_of_study", "weekend", "completion_time", "prompt_delay" )

# Focal variables from your substantive model (e.g., outcome and/or predictors)
focal_vars <- c("negative_affect", "physical_activity", "sedentary_behavior")

# Key identifiers
id_var <- "id"          # person identifier in your dataset
missing_var <- "missed_prompt" # prompt-level missingness (1 = missing, 0 = completed)

2.3 Step 3a: Data Readiness Check

What this does: Ensures all required names exist in the dataset.
Why it matters: Prevents cryptic errors later (e.g., misspellings or missing columns).

# 1) Verify dataset
if (!exists("ema_df")) {
  stop("❌ Dataset 'ema_df' not found. Please load or create it in Step 1 before proceeding.")
}
ema_df <- as.data.frame(ema_df)

# 2) Verify ID and missingness
if (!(id_var %in% names(ema_df))) {
  stop(paste0("❌ The ID variable '", id_var, "' was not found in ema_df."))
}
if (!(missing_var %in% names(ema_df))) {
  stop(paste0("❌ The missingness variable '", missing_var, "' was not found in ema_df."))
}

# 3) Check auxiliaries
missing_aux <- setdiff(aux_vars, names(ema_df))
if (length(missing_aux) > 0) {
  msg <- paste0("⚠️ The following auxiliary variable(s) were not found in ema_df and will be skipped: ",
                paste(missing_aux, collapse = ", "))
  cat("\n", msg, "\n")
  warning(msg, call. = FALSE)
  aux_vars <- intersect(aux_vars, names(ema_df))
}

# 4) Check focal variables
missing_focal <- setdiff(focal_vars, names(ema_df))
if (length(missing_focal) > 0) {
  msg <- paste0("⚠️ The following focal variable(s) were not found in ema_df and will be skipped: ",
                paste(missing_focal, collapse = ", "))
  cat("\n", msg, "\n")
  warning(msg, call. = FALSE)
  focal_vars <- intersect(focal_vars, names(ema_df))
}

# 5) Summary message
message("✅ Data readiness check completed successfully.")
## ✅ Data readiness check completed successfully.
message("  • Dataset dimensions: ", nrow(ema_df), " rows × ", ncol(ema_df), " columns")
##   • Dataset dimensions: 30 rows × 11 columns
message("  • ID variable: ", id_var)
##   • ID variable: id
message("  • Missingness variable: ", missing_var)
##   • Missingness variable: missed_prompt
message("  • Auxiliary variables (", length(aux_vars), "): ", paste(aux_vars, collapse = ", "))
##   • Auxiliary variables (5): time_of_day, day_of_study, weekend, completion_time, prompt_delay
message("  • Focal variables (", length(focal_vars), "): ", paste(focal_vars, collapse = ", "))
##   • Focal variables (3): negative_affect, physical_activity, sedentary_behavior

2.4 Step 3b: Compute ICCs for Each Auxiliary

What this does: Quantifies each auxiliary’s between-person proportion of variance.
Why it matters: We classify auxiliaries as pure_within (ICC < .05), pure_between (ICC > .95), or mixed.

icc_df <- data.frame()

for (var in aux_vars) {
  if (!var %in% names(ema_df)) next

  df_icc <- ema_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(id_var)) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(
      grp_mean = mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      grp_var  = var(.data[[var]],  na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  var_between <- var(df_icc$grp_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  var_within  <- mean(df_icc$grp_var, na.rm = TRUE)
  icc_val     <- var_between / (var_between + var_within)

  icc_df <- rbind(icc_df, data.frame(variable = var, ICC = icc_val))
}

ema_icc <- icc_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ICC = round(ICC, 3),
    classification = dplyr::case_when(
      ICC > .95 ~ "pure_between",
      ICC < .05 ~ "pure_within",
      TRUE      ~ "mixed"
    )
  )

ema_icc
##          variable   ICC classification
## 1     time_of_day 0.147          mixed
## 2    day_of_study 0.000    pure_within
## 3         weekend 0.134          mixed
## 4 completion_time 0.418          mixed
## 5    prompt_delay 0.110          mixed

2.5 Step 4: Center and Standardize Auxiliaries

What this does: Splits each auxiliary into within-person (WP) and between-person (PM) parts and standardizes them.
Why it matters: Multilevel models need correctly separated components to avoid conflating within- and between-person effects.

safe_sd <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)

for (var in aux_vars) {
  # Create person-mean and within-person deviations
  ema_df <- ema_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!rlang::sym(id_var)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      !!rlang::sym(paste0(var, "_PM")) := mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE),
      !!rlang::sym(paste0(var, "_WP")) := .data[[var]] - mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()

  # Standardize safely (leave NA when variance is zero)
  wp <- ema_df[[paste0(var, "_WP")]]
  pm <- ema_df[[paste0(var, "_PM")]]

  sd_wp <- safe_sd(wp)
  sd_pm <- safe_sd(pm)

  ema_df[[paste0(var, "_WP_z")]] <- if (!is.na(sd_wp) && sd_wp > 0) as.numeric(scale(wp)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(ema_df))
  ema_df[[paste0(var, "_PM_z")]] <- if (!is.na(sd_pm) && sd_pm > 0) as.numeric(scale(pm)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(ema_df))
}

2.6 Step 5: Predict Missingness (Multilevel Logistic Models)

What this does: For each auxiliary, estimates how strongly it predicts missingness at WP and/or PM level.
Output: Odds ratios (OR) by level.

logit_results <- data.frame()

for (var in aux_vars) {
  wp_col <- paste0(var, "_WP_z")
  pm_col <- paste0(var, "_PM_z")

  df_sub <- ema_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[missing_var]]) & (!is.na(.data[[wp_col]]) | !is.na(.data[[pm_col]])))

  if (nrow(df_sub) < 20) {
    warning(paste("Skipping", var, "- fewer than 20 usable rows."))
    next
  }

  rhs <- c()
  if (any(!is.na(df_sub[[wp_col]]))) rhs <- c(rhs, wp_col)
  if (any(!is.na(df_sub[[pm_col]]))) rhs <- c(rhs, pm_col)

  # Random intercept by person
  fml <- reformulate(termlabels = c(rhs, paste0("(1|", "`", id_var, "`", ")")), response = missing_var)

  model <- tryCatch(lme4::glmer(fml, data = df_sub, family = binomial, nAGQ = 0),
                    error = function(e) NULL)

  if (!is.null(model)) {
    ests <- broom.mixed::tidy(model, effects = "fixed")
    ests <- ests[ests$term != "(Intercept)", ]
    ests$level <- ifelse(grepl("_WP_z$", ests$term), "within", "between")
    ests$variable <- var
    ests$OR <- exp(ests$estimate)
    logit_results <- rbind(logit_results, ests[, c("variable","level","OR")])
  }
}

2.7 Step 6: Correlate Auxiliaries with Focal Variables

What this does: Computes signed within- and between-person correlations of each auxiliary with each focal variable.
Why it matters: Auxiliaries useful for imputation should relate meaningfully to model variables.

cor_results <- data.frame()

for (aux in aux_vars) {
  if (!aux %in% names(ema_df)) {
    warning(paste("Variable", aux, "not found; skipping."))
    next
  }

  for (foc in focal_vars) {
    if (!foc %in% names(ema_df)) {
      warning(paste("Variable", foc, "not found; skipping."))
      next
    }

    x_aux <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ema_df[[aux]]))
    x_foc <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ema_df[[foc]]))
    g     <- as.vector(ema_df[[id_var]])

    df_sub <- data.frame(aux = x_aux, foc = x_foc, g = g)
    df_sub <- df_sub[!is.na(df_sub$aux) & !is.na(df_sub$foc), ]

    if (nrow(df_sub) == 0) {
      warning(paste("No valid data for pair", aux, "and", foc, "; skipping."))
      next
    }

    # Within-person correlation (de-mean by person)
    aux_WP <- df_sub$aux - ave(df_sub$aux, df_sub$g, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
    foc_WP <- df_sub$foc - ave(df_sub$foc, df_sub$g, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
    cor_w  <- suppressWarnings(cor(aux_WP, foc_WP, use = "pairwise"))

    # Between-person correlation (person means)
    df_bp <- aggregate(cbind(aux = df_sub$aux, foc = df_sub$foc), by = list(df_sub$g), FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
    cor_b <- suppressWarnings(cor(df_bp$aux, df_bp$foc, use = "pairwise"))

    cor_results <- rbind(
      cor_results,
      data.frame(variable = aux, level = "within",  focal_var = foc, correlation = cor_w),
      data.frame(variable = aux, level = "between", focal_var = foc, correlation = cor_b)
    )
  }
}

2.8 Step 7: Interactive Detailed Table

What this shows: Each auxiliary variable appears once per level (within and/or between). Pure within-person variables appear only with Level = “within.” Pure between-person variables appear only with Level = “between.” Mixed variables appear twice, once per level. Columns show the variable’s association with missingness (OR) and with each focal variable (correlations r).

# 1) Merge correlation and logistic results
detailed_df <- cor_results %>%
  dplyr::left_join(logit_results, by = c("variable", "level")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(ema_icc, by = "variable")

# 2) Mask irrelevant level-components based on ICC classification
detailed_df <- detailed_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    OR = dplyr::if_else(classification == "pure_within"  & level == "between", NA_real_, OR),
    OR = dplyr::if_else(classification == "pure_between" & level == "within",  NA_real_, OR),
    correlation = dplyr::if_else(classification == "pure_within"  & level == "between", NA_real_, correlation),
    correlation = dplyr::if_else(classification == "pure_between" & level == "within",  NA_real_, correlation)
  )

# 3) Pivot correlations so focal variables become side-by-side columns
wide_cor <- detailed_df %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, level, focal_var, correlation) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = focal_var,
    values_from = correlation,
    names_glue = "{focal_var}_r"
  )

# 4) Merge ORs and keep only relevant info (no ICC/classification)
wide_combined <- wide_cor %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    detailed_df %>%
      dplyr::select(variable, level, OR) %>%
      dplyr::distinct(),
    by = c("variable", "level")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(variable, level, OR, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    OR  = round(OR, 3),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::matches("_r$"), ~ round(.x, 3))
  )

# 5) Drop level-rows where all numeric columns are NA
wide_combined <- wide_combined %>%
  dplyr::filter(rowSums(!is.na(dplyr::select(., where(is.numeric)))) > 0)

# 6) Tidy up labels and order
wide_combined <- wide_combined %>%
  dplyr::arrange(variable, dplyr::desc(level)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `Auxiliary Variable` = variable,
    `Level` = level,
    `Missingness (OR)` = OR
  )

# 7) Display interactive datatable
DT::datatable(
  wide_combined,
  extensions = "Scroller",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 50,
    scrollX = TRUE,
    deferRender = TRUE,
    dom = 'tip',
    columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-center', targets = "_all"))
  ),
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = 'caption-side: top; text-align: left;',
    htmltools::tags$strong("Detailed overview of auxiliary variables by level."),
    htmltools::tags$br(),
    "Each variable appears once per relevant level (within and/or between).",
    htmltools::tags$br(),
    "Columns show odds ratios (OR) for missingness and correlations (r) with each focal variable."
  )
)

3 *Step 8: Visual Heatmap of Auxiliary Variable Strength**

What this shows: This heatmap summarizes all quantitative evidence about each auxiliary variable in a single, intuitive visual format. The heatmap highlights the pattern and magnitude of associations across:

  • Missingness prediction (odds ratios converted to r-equivalent effect sizes)
  • Correlations with each focal variable

Each auxiliary variable appears with both within-person and between-person components whenever those levels exist: * Pure within-person auxiliaries show only within tiles * Pure between-person auxiliaries show only between tiles * Mixed auxiliaries show a full set of tiles at both levels

This visualization allows you to quickly evaluate which auxiliaries show meaningfully sized relationships—and at which levels. It supports empirically grounded decisions about which auxiliary variables to include in your model.

## Step 8: Split-Panel Dual Heatmap (Missingness vs. Focal Variables)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# -------------------------------
# Helper: mask by classification
# -------------------------------

mask_by_classification <- function(df, class_df) {
  df %>%
    left_join(class_df %>% select(variable, classification), by = "variable") %>%
    mutate(
      abs_r = case_when(
        classification == "pure_within"  & level == "between" ~ NA_real_,
        classification == "pure_between" & level == "within"  ~ NA_real_,
        TRUE                                                    ~ abs_r
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-classification)
}

# -------------------------------
# Helper: OR → r-equivalent
# -------------------------------
to_r_from_logOR <- function(OR) {
  logOR <- log(OR)
  d     <- logOR * sqrt(3) / pi
  d / sqrt(d^2 + 4)
}

# -------------------------------
# 0. Common pieces: variables, labels
# -------------------------------

# Ensure we have a clean list of auxiliaries from ICC object
aux_vars_all <- ema_icc$variable

# Make a readable axis label that includes ICC
ema_icc <- ema_icc %>%
  mutate(
    icc_label = ifelse(
      is.na(ICC), 
      paste0(variable, " (ICC = NA)"),
      paste0(variable, " (ICC = ", sprintf("%.2f", ICC), ")")
    )
  )

# Fix ordering of auxiliaries (same for both panels)
aux_order <- ema_icc$icc_label

# -------------------------------
# Panel 1: Missingness predictors
# -------------------------------

# Full grid: every variable x level
miss_grid <- expand.grid(
  variable = aux_vars_all,
  level    = c("within", "between"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# OR → |r|
logit_r <- logit_results %>%
  mutate(
    abs_r = abs(to_r_from_logOR(OR))
  ) %>%
  select(variable, level, abs_r)

# Merge grid and data, attach ICC + label
miss_df <- miss_grid %>%
  left_join(logit_r, by = c("variable", "level")) %>%
    mask_by_classification(ema_icc) %>%   # <— ENFORCE PURE WITHIN/BETWEEN
  left_join(ema_icc, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(
    aux_label = factor(icc_label, levels = aux_order)
  )

# Bin effect sizes for missingness (Option A thresholds)
miss_df <- miss_df %>%
  mutate(
    bin = case_when(
      is.na(abs_r)        ~ "NA",
      abs_r < 0.05        ~ "< .05",
      abs_r < 0.10        ~ ".05–.10",
      abs_r < 0.20        ~ ".10–.20",
      abs_r >= 0.20       ~ "> .20"
    ),
    bin = factor(bin, levels = c("< .05", ".05–.10", ".10–.20", "> .20", "NA"))
  )

# Gold palette for missingness
palette_miss <- c(
  "< .05"   = "white",
  ".05–.10" = "#FFE599",  # pale gold
  ".10–.20" = "#FFC000",  # medium gold
  "> .20"   = "#C65911",  # deep amber
  "NA"      = "#CCCCCC"   # gray for structural NA
)

p_missing <- ggplot(miss_df, aes(x = level, y = aux_label, fill = bin)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey70") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = palette_miss,
    name   = "Abs(r) from OR\n(missingness)"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    x = "Level",
    y = NULL,
    title    = "Missingness Prediction"
   # subtitle = "Odds ratios converted to r-equivalent effect sizes (absolute value)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14,face = "bold"),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold.italic")
  )

# -------------------------------
# Panel 2: Correlations with focal variables
# -------------------------------

# Full grid: every auxiliary × level × focal_var
cor_grid <- expand.grid(
  variable  = aux_vars_all,
  level     = c("between", "within"),   # consistent level order
  focal_var = focal_vars,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Absolute correlations
corr_r <- cor_results %>%
  mutate(abs_r = abs(correlation)) %>%
  select(variable, level, focal_var, abs_r)

# Merge + ICC labels
cor_df <- cor_grid %>%
  left_join(corr_r, by = c("variable", "level", "focal_var")) %>%
    mask_by_classification(ema_icc) %>%   # <— ENFORCE PURE WITHIN/BETWEEN
  left_join(ema_icc, by = "variable") %>%
  mutate(
    aux_label = factor(icc_label, levels = aux_order),
    metric_raw = paste(focal_var, level, sep = "_")
  )

# -------------------------------
# NEW: Correct desired ordering
# -------------------------------

# First all "between", then all "within", WITHIN each focal variable
metric_levels <- c(
  paste0(focal_vars, "_between"),
  paste0(focal_vars, "_within")
)

cor_df <- cor_df %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_raw, levels = metric_levels))

# -------------------------------
# Binning effect sizes
# -------------------------------
cor_df <- cor_df %>%
  mutate(
    bin = case_when(
      is.na(abs_r)        ~ "NA",
      abs_r < 0.10        ~ "< .10",
      abs_r < 0.20        ~ ".10–.20",
      abs_r < 0.40        ~ ".20–.40",
      abs_r >= 0.40       ~ "> .40"
    ),
    bin = factor(bin, levels = c("< .10", ".10–.20", ".20–.40", "> .40", "NA"))
  )

# -------------------------------
# Blue palette for correlation heatmap
# -------------------------------
palette_cor <- c(
  "< .10"   = "white",
  ".10–.20" = "#C6DBEF",
  ".20–.40" = "#6BAED6",
  "> .40"   = "#08519C",
  "NA"      = "#CCCCCC"
)

# -------------------------------
# Panel 2 Plot
# -------------------------------
p_cor <- ggplot(cor_df, aes(x = metric, y = aux_label, fill = bin)) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey70") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = palette_cor,
    name   = "Abs(r)\nwith focal variables"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    title    = "Correlations with Focal Variables"
   # subtitle = "Between-person effects shown first, followed by within-person"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0, hjust = 0, size = 10),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot", 
    plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold.italic")
  )

# -------------------------------
# Combine panels vertically
# -------------------------------

combo <- (p_missing / p_cor + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(.9, 1)))

# 1. Calculate height inside the code
n_vars <- length(unique(miss_df$variable))
h <- 3 + (n_vars * 2 * 0.2)

# 2. Save explicitly to a file
ggsave("heatmap.png", 
       plot = combo, 
       width = 10, 
       height = h, 
       limitsize = FALSE)

# 3. Import the file back into the markdown
knitr::include_graphics("heatmap.png")

4 Wrap-Up

You now have two complementary views:

  1. Interactive detailed table — Explore ORs and signed correlations for each auxiliary × focal combination, with within/between side by side.
  2. Visual heatmap — Prioritize auxiliaries by the strength of their relationships with missingness and focal variables on a common r-scale.

Use both quantitative evidence and conceptual reasoning when deciding which auxiliaries to include.
The goal is to capture variables that meaningfully explain the missingness process and align with your substantive model.

4.1 Appendix: Troubleshooting Tips

  • If you see warnings in Step 3a, double-check variable names in Step 2.
  • If a variable is pure_within (ICC < .05), between-level entries are set to NA by design.
  • If a variable is pure_between (ICC > .95), within-level entries are set to NA by design.
  • Logistic models in Step 5 require at least ~20 usable rows per auxiliary; otherwise they are skipped.
